title: Selection sort
summary: On each pass select the smallest element in the unsorted range and swap it with the first, extending the sorted prefix by one element.
context: The goal is to sort nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2] in nondecreasing order. There are 6 elements with indices 0 through 5.

On each pass, i points to the first element of the unsorted range and k records the index of its minimum. Green cells form the unsorted range, marked by a brace above. Gray cells on the left form the sorted prefix. Once k is chosen, swap nums[k] and nums[i] to extend the prefix one place to the right.
description: The first ten of eleven frames show five passes in pairs. The selection frame gives i and k after scanning, omitting individual comparisons in the inner loop. The swap frame shows the resulting array and marks the exchanged positions with arcs above and below; the labels i and k disappear. The eleventh frame leaves one element, so a sixth pass is unnecessary.

frames.title: Select the minimum 1 at index 1
frames.explanation: Pass 1, selection: nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2]. After scanning [0, 5], i = 0 points to the first element 4 and k = 1 to the minimum 1. The two 1s are at indices 1 and 3. With a strict less-than comparison, k = 1 keeps the leftmost one. The sorted prefix is empty. No swap yet.
frames.key_state: Pass 1, minimum selected, no swap yet. nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2]; unsorted range [0, 5], i = 0, k = 1, minimum 1.
frames.announcement: Pass 1 selects the minimum 1 at index k = 1 in [0, 5].

frames.title: Swap indices 0 and 1
frames.explanation: Pass 1, swap: in [0, 5], swap the minimum 1 at index 1 with the first element 4 at index 0. Now nums = [1, 4, 3, 1, 5, 2]. The gray sorted prefix [1] occupies index 0. The unsorted range [1, 5] contains [4, 3, 1, 5, 2].
frames.key_state: Pass 1, swap complete. nums = [1, 4, 3, 1, 5, 2]; index 0 is settled. Unsorted range [1, 5].
frames.announcement: Swap 4 at index 0 with 1 at index 1, fixing 1 at index 0.

frames.title: Select the minimum 1 at index 3
frames.explanation: Pass 2, selection: nums = [1, 4, 3, 1, 5, 2]. After scanning [1, 5], i = 1 points to the first element 4 and k = 3 to the minimum 1. The sorted prefix occupies index 0 and contains [1]. No swap yet.
frames.key_state: Pass 2, minimum selected, no swap yet. nums = [1, 4, 3, 1, 5, 2]; unsorted range [1, 5], i = 1, k = 3, minimum 1.
frames.announcement: Pass 2 selects the minimum 1 at index k = 3 in [1, 5].

frames.title: Swap indices 1 and 3
frames.explanation: Pass 2, swap: in [1, 5], swap the minimum 1 at index 3 with the first element 4 at index 1. Now nums = [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 2]. The gray sorted prefix [1, 1] occupies indices 0 through 1. The unsorted range [2, 5] contains [3, 4, 5, 2].
frames.key_state: Pass 2, swap complete. nums = [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 2]; indices 0 through 1 are settled. Unsorted range [2, 5].
frames.announcement: Swap 4 at index 1 with 1 at index 3, fixing the second 1 at index 1.

frames.title: Select the minimum 2 at index 5
frames.explanation: Pass 3, selection: nums = [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 2]. After scanning [2, 5], i = 2 points to the first element 3 and k = 5 to the minimum 2. The sorted prefix occupies indices 0 through 1 and contains [1, 1]. No swap yet.
frames.key_state: Pass 3, minimum selected, no swap yet. nums = [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 2]; unsorted range [2, 5], i = 2, k = 5, minimum 2.
frames.announcement: Pass 3 selects the minimum 2 at index k = 5 in [2, 5].

frames.title: Swap indices 2 and 5
frames.explanation: Pass 3, swap: in [2, 5], swap the minimum 2 at index 5 with the first element 3 at index 2. Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 3]. The gray sorted prefix [1, 1, 2] occupies indices 0 through 2. The unsorted range [3, 5] contains [4, 5, 3].
frames.key_state: Pass 3, swap complete. nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 3]; indices 0 through 2 are settled. Unsorted range [3, 5].
frames.announcement: Swap 3 at index 2 with 2 at index 5, fixing 2 at index 2.

frames.title: Select the minimum 3 at index 5
frames.explanation: Pass 4, selection: nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 3]. After scanning [3, 5], i = 3 points to the first element 4 and k = 5 to the minimum 3. The sorted prefix occupies indices 0 through 2 and contains [1, 1, 2]. No swap yet.
frames.key_state: Pass 4, minimum selected, no swap yet. nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 3]; unsorted range [3, 5], i = 3, k = 5, minimum 3.
frames.announcement: Pass 4 selects the minimum 3 at index k = 5 in [3, 5].

frames.title: Swap indices 3 and 5

frames.key_state: Pass 4, swap complete. nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 4]; indices 0 through 3 are settled. Unsorted range [4, 5].
frames.announcement: Swap 4 at index 3 with 3 at index 5, fixing 3 at index 3.

frames.title: Select the minimum 4 at index 5
frames.explanation: Pass 5, selection: nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 4]. After scanning [4, 5], i = 4 points to the first element 5 and k = 5 to the minimum 4. The sorted prefix occupies indices 0 through 3 and contains [1, 1, 2, 3]. No swap yet.
frames.key_state: Pass 5, minimum selected, no swap yet. nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 4]; unsorted range [4, 5], i = 4, k = 5, minimum 4.

frames.title: Swap indices 4 and 5

frames.key_state: Pass 5, swap complete. nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; indices 0 through 4 are settled. Unsorted range [5, 5].
frames.announcement: Swap 5 at index 4 with 4 at index 5, fixing 4 at index 4.

frames.title: Sorting complete
frames.explanation: After five passes nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The gray sorted prefix occupies indices 0 through 4. The green 5 at index 5 is still shown in the singleton unsorted range [5, 5]. As the maximum, it is already in the correct position. The figure reads “Sorting complete (the remaining element needs no sorting).” Both i and k are hidden.
frames.key_state: Five passes complete. The final element 5 is already in place, giving the sorted array [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
frames.announcement: Only the last element 5 remains. No more selections are needed; selection sort is complete.
